_meta.purpose: Left-panel documentation for tomogration, keyed by STAGES[].id. Wire each stage's docs from here (replace the inline 'docs' dicts in tomogration_app.py, or load this JSON at startup).
_meta.render_hint: Per stage show: title, what, why, a parameter table (name / flag / default / range / effect), then pitfalls (red), qc (what good output looks like), and refs as clickable links.
_meta.dataset_context: EER, 1.57 A/px unbinned, ~3.5 e/A2 per tilt, FIB lamella, V100 GPUs. Defaults below are official-guide values adapted for this pixel size/dose; treat as starting points.

create_settings_fs.title: create_settings (frame series)
create_settings_fs.what: Creates warp_frameseries.settings, the file every later frame-series command reads. Defines raw pixel size, gain reference, dose and EER frame grouping for the whole project.
create_settings_fs.why: All downstream geometry and dose-weighting derive from these values. Set once, correctly, or every later step is subtly wrong.

params.name: angpix
params.effect: Raw UNBINNED pixel size. Must match the detector, not any binned value.

params.name: gain_path
params.effect: Gain reference. Pair with --gain_flip_y / --gain_flip_x / --gain_transpose to match detector orientation.

params.name: exposure
params.effect: Dose in e/A2 per tilt (or per frame depending on convention) used for dose-weighting.

params.name: eer_ngroups
params.effect: How EER frames are grouped into fractions. Too few = poor motion fit; too many = noisy fractions. Match to dose/frame.

params.name: extension
params.effect: Raw file pattern.

create_settings_fs.pitfalls: Pixel size is the raw unbinned value. Wrong gain flip => streaky averages. EER grouping is easy to forget and hard to spot later.
create_settings_fs.qc: Averages in warp_frameseries/average should look clean and un-streaked; CTF Thon rings visible in previews.

fs_motion_and_ctf.title: fs_motion_and_ctf
fs_motion_and_ctf.what: Per-frame-series motion correction plus CTF estimation. Produces motion-corrected averages (and odd/even half-sets) and per-micrograph CTF.
fs_motion_and_ctf.why: Motion-corrected averages are the input to tilt-series alignment; the CTF estimate feeds dose-weighting and later 3D-CTF handling. Half-sets enable Noise2Noise denoising.

params.name: m_grid
params.effect: Motion model resolution. First two = spatial (local motion), third = temporal (~ frame/fraction count). Higher temporal costs lots of memory for little gain.

params.name: c_grid
params.effect: CTF/defocus model resolution. 5x5 suits 4K at 1.0-1.3 A/px; at 1.57 A/px, 2x2-3x3 is usually enough. Temporal >1 rarely helps.

params.name: m_range_min
params.effect: Low-res bound of the motion fit.

params.name: m_range_max
params.effect: High-res bound of the motion fit.

params.name: m_bfac
params.effect: B-factor downweighting high frequencies. More negative = stronger low-pass, more robust on low-SNR data.

params.name: c_range_max
params.effect: High-res bound for CTF fit. Lower prevents overfitting a high-res defocus model.

params.name: c_defocus_max
params.effect: Upper defocus bound of the exhaustive search. Match acquisition range plus margin.

params.name: c_use_sum
params.effect: Fit CTF from the motion-corrected average rather than per-frame spectra. Helps when per-frame signal is low or there is no energy filter.

params.name: out_averages
params.effect: Write aligned averages (needed for alignment).

params.name: out_average_halves
params.effect: Write odd/even half-averages (needed for Noise2Noise denoising of images/tomograms).

fs_motion_and_ctf.pitfalls: Auto-recovery quarantines a bad .eer to frames/bad/, removes its mdoc ZValue block, logs it, and retries. Only fs_* auto-recovers; ts_* crashes are GPU/resource, not bad files. cuFFT crashes here usually mean one corrupt frame, not a parameter problem.
fs_motion_and_ctf.qc: Use ts_filter_quality / filter_quality to print CTF-resolution and motion histograms. Outliers in CTF resolution flag bad tilts.

ts_import.title: ts_import
ts_import.what: Tells WarpTools which movies belong to which tilt series, using the mdocs, and writes .tomostar files (one per series) carrying tilt angles and cumulative dose.
ts_import.why: Establishes per-tilt dose bookkeeping and geometric handedness before any alignment.

params.name: tilt_exposure
params.effect: Per-tilt dose (e/A2) for cumulative-dose tracking.

params.name: min_intensity
params.effect: Drops tilts darker than min_intensity * cos(tilt) * 0-tilt intensity. Removes blocked/grid-bar tilts.

params.name: dont_invert
params.effect: Inverts geometric handedness by flipping through XY. Whether you need it depends on the scope/camera path; verify with ts_defocus_hand.

ts_import.pitfalls: If an .eer was quarantined but its mdoc ZValue block was NOT removed, ts_import fails with 'failed to parse specific tilts'. Use Repair mdocs to fix stale entries.
ts_import.qc: One .tomostar per series in tomostar/; tilt counts match expectation after exclusions.

ts_stack.title: ts_stack
ts_stack.what: Generates aligned tilt-series stacks (.mrc) plus IMOD-format .rawtlt files at a chosen pixel size, ready for an external aligner.
ts_stack.why: Alignment programs (AreTomo2, IMOD/Etomo) operate on these stacks. Masked regions are filled with statistics-matched Gaussian noise to aid alignment.

params.name: angpix
params.effect: Working pixel size for alignment. Coarser = faster and more robust for fiducial-less alignment; you re-reconstruct finer later.

ts_stack.pitfalls: Run ts_import first. The angpix here defines the space your .xf alignments live in; ts_import_alignments must use the same value.
ts_stack.qc: Stacks in tiltstack/<TS>/ open cleanly in 3dmod; tilt order monotonic.

aretomo.title: AreTomo2 (ts_aretomo)
aretomo.what: GPU, marker-free tilt-series alignment (and optional reconstruction). Solves tilt-axis, shifts and local motion, then exports IMOD-style .xf transforms for Warp to import.
aretomo.why: Lamella data has no fiducials; AreTomo2 aligns without them. Alignment quality caps every downstream resolution.

params.name: angpix
params.effect: Alignment pixel size; match ts_stack.

params.name: alignz
params.effect: Z-height searched during alignment. Set near the true sample thickness in pixels. For FIB lamellae, use the known lamella thickness.

params.name: tilt_axis
params.effect: Initial tilt-axis angle. Provide if auto-search drifts; AreTomo can iterate it.

params.name: axis_iter
params.effect: Iterations refining the tilt axis.

params.name: patch
params.effect: Local patch alignment grid. More patches model local deformation but need signal; 0 0 = global only.

params.name: dark_tol
params.effect: Threshold for discarding dark tilts.

params.name: out_imod
params.effect: Write IMOD-format output so Warp can import .xf alignments.

aretomo.pitfalls: Wrong AlignZ is the most common cause of poor lamella alignment. Keep versioned output folders + a PARAMETERS.txt audit per run so you can compare. Smaller tilt increments tend to align better and improve tomogram SNR despite weaker per-tilt signal.
aretomo.qc: Check the alignment residual/score AreTomo reports; reconstruct a quick binned tomogram and look for 'ghosting'/drift in 3dmod (a sign of bad alignment).

ts_import_alignments.title: ts_import_alignments
ts_import_alignments.what: Imports the external aligner's .xf transforms back into the WarpTools project.
ts_import_alignments.why: Lets Warp reconstruct and export particles using alignments solved by AreTomo2/IMOD.

params.name: alignment_angpix
params.effect: Pixel size the alignments were computed at. MUST equal the ts_stack/AreTomo angpix or geometry is scaled wrong.

ts_import_alignments.pitfalls: Mismatched alignment_angpix silently corrupts geometry. Use 'Sync selection with alignments' to deselect series lacking a matching .xf before reconstruct.
ts_import_alignments.qc: Every selected .tomostar has a corresponding imported alignment.

ts_defocus_hand.title: ts_defocus_hand
ts_defocus_hand.what: Checks (and optionally sets) the defocus handedness of the tilt series.
ts_defocus_hand.why: Wrong defocus handedness ruins 3D-CTF correction and caps resolution. Run --check before final CTF; --set_flip if it reports inverted.

params.name: check
params.effect: Reports a correlation score; negative score => handedness is flipped.

params.name: set_flip
params.effect: Applies the flip when the check reports inverted.

ts_defocus_hand.pitfalls: ts_ctf --auto_hand N can auto-detect/flip during CTF; reports of a stale 'still inverted' message after flipping are a known cosmetic quirk. Decide handedness once, then keep it fixed.

ts_ctf.title: ts_ctf
ts_ctf.what: Per-tilt CTF estimation that enforces constraints common to the whole series (one defocus per image, consistent across tilts).
ts_ctf.why: Accurate per-tilt defocus is required for 3D-CTF-correct reconstruction and high-resolution averaging.

params.name: window
params.effect: Power-spectrum patch size. Small window = more local defocus, less spectral detail.

params.name: range_low
params.effect: Ignore lowest spatial frequencies in the fit.

params.name: range_high
params.effect: High-res bound of the fit.

params.name: defocus_min
params.effect: Lower bound of defocus search.

params.name: defocus_max
params.effect: Upper bound; match acquisition range plus margin.

params.name: voltage
params.effect: Microscope-fixed.

params.name: cs
params.effect: Spherical aberration; microscope-fixed.

params.name: amplitude
params.effect: Amplitude-contrast fraction.

params.name: auto_hand
params.effect: If set to the number of series, auto-checks/corrects defocus handedness during CTF.

ts_ctf.pitfalls: Run ts_defocus_hand first (or use --auto_hand). Overfitting a high-res model with too-high range_high is a common error.
ts_ctf.qc: ts_filter_quality histogram of CTF-resolution; flag series with poor fits and deselect.

ts_reconstruct.title: ts_reconstruct
ts_reconstruct.what: Back-projects aligned, CTF-corrected tilts into 3D tomograms, written to warp_tiltseries/reconstruction with preview slices.
ts_reconstruct.why: Tomograms are what you pick particles in and visually QC alignment. Reconstruct at a coarse pixel size for picking/inspection.

params.name: angpix
params.effect: Tomogram pixel size. Finer = bigger/slower volumes; coarse is fine for template matching and inspection.

params.name: perdevice
params.effect: Worker processes per GPU. KEEP AT 1 when --deconv is on (V100).

params.name: dont_invert
params.effect: Skip contrast inversion; choose so particles are dark-on-light consistently.

params.name: deconv
params.effect: Deconvolution filter for VISUAL contrast/inspection only. Do not use for the volumes you average from.

ts_reconstruct.pitfalls: --perdevice 2 with --deconv crashes on V100 (SIGABRT, cuFFT collision). Warp writes mode-12 float16 MRC; IMOD/Dynamo may choke ('Unknown file mrc_file_type 12'). Prepend WARP_FORCE_MRC_FLOAT32=1 to get float32. Set tomogram XY dimensions with the tilt axis along Y.
ts_reconstruct.qc: Open in 3dmod: sharp, non-ghosting features = good alignment. SART/SIRT look higher-contrast for viewing; WBP preserves high-frequency info better for STA.

ts_template_match.title: ts_template_match
ts_template_match.what: CTF-aware template matching to locate particles in tomograms, scoring each position against a rotated 3D reference.
ts_template_match.why: Automated picking. Output is a per-tomogram score volume + peaks you then threshold into a particle star file.

params.name: tomo_angpix
params.effect: Matching pixel size. Finer = more sensitive but much slower.

params.name: subdivisions
params.effect: Angular search step: 2 = 15 deg, 3 = 7.5 deg, 4 = 3.75 deg. Finer = slower, better for low-symmetry targets.

params.name: template_emdb
params.effect: Reference map. Use --template for a local .mrc.

params.name: template_diameter
params.effect: Particle diameter; sets the mask and peak spacing.

params.name: symmetry
params.effect: Reduces angular search; set the true symmetry (e.g. O for apoferritin).

params.name: whiten
params.effect: Spectral whitening boosts high-frequency contribution; helps when alignments are good.

params.name: check_hand
params.effect: Verifies geometric handedness by scoring template vs flipped template on N tomograms.

ts_template_match.pitfalls: Use --perdevice 1 for matching. Garbage in, garbage out: a bad-handedness or misaligned tomogram gives meaningless scores.
ts_template_match.qc: Overlay peaks on the tomogram in a viewer; peaks should sit on real densities, not ice/edges.

threshold_picks.title: threshold_picks
threshold_picks.what: Converts template-match score peaks into a cleaned particle star file by applying a score cutoff.
threshold_picks.why: Scores are normalised to background mean/SD, so the threshold is comparable across tomograms.

params.name: minimum
params.effect: Keep peaks at least N standard deviations above background. Higher = fewer false positives, may miss real particles.

params.name: in_suffix
params.effect: Match the suffix written by ts_template_match.

params.name: out_suffix
params.effect: Suffix for the thresholded output star files.

threshold_picks.pitfalls: Start conservative (high minimum), inspect, then relax. The guide uses values up to 6 SD.
threshold_picks.qc: Particle counts per tomogram are plausible; a 2D/3D classification later should yield clean class averages.

ts_export_particles.title: ts_export_particles
ts_export_particles.what: Extracts CTF-corrected particles from the original tilt images at a chosen pixel size and box, writing a RELION-compatible optimisation_set.star.
ts_export_particles.why: Extracts the particles into a RELION project directory. Choose 3D subtomograms for RELION 4 (--3d) or the 2D image series for RELION 5 --tomo. The subtomo image paths are written RELATIVE to output_processing, so RELION must be launched from that directory. For RELION 4, continue in the 'RELION 4: Class3D' step.

params.name: input_directory
params.effect: Where the thresholded pick stars live.

params.name: input_pattern
params.effect: Which pick files to export.

params.name: output_angpix
params.effect: Export pixel size. Choose so Nyquist sits just below your target feature resolution.

params.name: box
params.effect: Box size in px at output_angpix. Must comfortably contain the particle plus padding.

params.name: diameter
params.effect: Particle diameter for normalisation.

params.name: relion_format
params.effect: Exactly one is required: --3d = 3D subtomogram volumes (RELION 4); --2d = 2D image series (RELION 5 --tomo).

params.name: normalized_coords
params.effect: Coordinates normalised to tomogram dimensions.

params.name: relative_output_paths
params.effect: Portable relative paths in the star file.

params.name: output_processing
params.effect: Redirect output to a per-target folder so different particle sets at the same pixel size don't overwrite each other.

ts_export_particles.pitfalls: Without --output_processing, exporting two targets at the same pixel size can overwrite files in particleseries/subtomo. The produced optimisation_set.star loads directly in relion --tomo.
ts_export_particles.qc: Open the optimisation set in RELION 5 tomo GUI; particle count and pixel size match expectation.
ts_export_particles.pitfall: LAUNCH RELION FROM output_processing or every subtomo path is wrong ('file does not exist'). Keep --relative_output_paths ON. RELION 4 does NOT auto-resize the reference — the RELION 4 step pre-scales it for you.

relion4_convert.title: RELION 4: convert STAR + init ref
relion4_convert.what: Converts the Warp ts_export_particles star to RELION 4 format and builds a de-novo initial reference, via ml_relion4_convert_star_warp_auto.sh.
relion4_convert.why: Bridges ts_export_particles and Class3D. It rewrites the relative 'subtomo/' particle paths to absolute (so RELION resolves every subtomogram), runs relion_convert_star (adds Cs/Q0 optics), then samples NREF random particles and relion_reconstructs random_subset_ref.mrc — a ready-made reference so you don't need an external EMDB map. The STAR header is split by auto-detecting the last '_rln' label (replaces the original script's hardcoded head -n 33 / tail -n +35).

params.name: project_dir
params.effect: The ts_export_particles output_processing dir; relion runs from here.

params.name: starfile
params.effect: The Warp export star to convert.

params.name: PARTICLEDIR
params.effect: Replaces the 'subtomo/' prefix in the star so RELION finds the particles.

params.name: PATH_MATCH
params.effect: The prefix in the Warp star to rewrite. Change only if export wrote a different one.

params.name: CS / Q0
params.effect: Spherical aberration (mm) and amplitude contrast for relion_convert_star.

params.name: NREF
params.effect: Random particles used to reconstruct the initial reference.

params.name: MAKE_REF
params.effect: 1 = also build random_subset_ref.mrc; 0 = only convert the star.

params.name: execute
params.effect: Off = dry run (prints the plan + relion commands). On = actually convert + reconstruct.

relion4_convert.pitfall: Runs FROM project_dir (paths are relative to it). PATH_MATCH must match how export wrote the paths or the rewrite is a no-op and RELION can't find the particles. Feed random_subset_ref.mrc into the Class3D step as REF_MAP with REF_ANGPIX = the export output_angpix (it is already at particle scale).

relion4_class3d.title: RELION 4: Class3D handoff
relion4_class3d.what: Hands the exported 3D subtomograms to RELION 4 for 3D classification, via ml_relion4_handoff_warp_auto.sh.
relion4_class3d.why: Encodes the fragile parts of the Warp->RELION handoff: it asserts the export is complete and that the star's subtomo paths resolve from the project dir, pre-scales the reference to the particles' pixel size + box (RELION 4 has no auto-resize), parks any stale cross-version pipeline files, and submits Class3D with MPI = #GPUs+1, run FROM the project directory.

params.name: project_dir
params.effect: The ts_export_particles output_processing dir; relion runs from here.

params.name: REF_MAP
params.effect: Reference map (e.g. the EMDB map). Rescaled to match the particles.

params.name: OUTPUT_ANGPIX / BOX
params.effect: MUST equal the ts_export_particles output_angpix and box.

params.name: SYMMETRY
params.effect: Classify in C1; symmetrise only at Refine3D.

params.name: NCLASSES
params.effect: Number of 3D classes.

params.name: GPUS
params.effect: RELION GPUs; MPI is set to #GPUs+1 automatically.

params.name: execute
params.effect: Off = dry run (prints the plan + relion command). On = actually submit.

relion4_class3d.pitfall: RELION 4 is the GPU-native path on this VM class (RELION 5's container CUDA can outrun the host driver -> GPU error-code 35). OUTPUT_ANGPIX/BOX must match the export. Never launch inside another RELION version's project.
